text:
emily-sales: Heads-up — Heartwood reopened the SIG with follow-ups specifically around BCP/DR and reliability controls. They want: RTO/RPO numbers by deployment type, backup cadence, cross-region failover steps, a short SLA summary, and evidence (runbook + last test). Can we assemble by EOD?

ryan-infra: I have the runbook and the post-mortem from the last failover test. Will pull a succinct summary. Note: RTO/RPO vary by deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

morgan-eng: Quick tech notes to prepare for wording: multi-AZ frontends, stateful KV replication for metadata, continuous backups for DBs, and async cross-region DR for logs. Cache/KV best-effort recovery semantics are important to call out.

jaime-sales: Customer specifically asked for: 
- RTO expectations for API endpoints 
- RPO for customer data and logs 
- Evidence of a successful failover drill (date + duration)
- A plain-language SLA blurb we can paste into their vendor risk portal.

ryan-infra: Draft numbers from infra: 
- Hosted API (managed): target RTO = 15 minutes for routing + warm standby rehydration; typical observed full recovery ~10–25 minutes during tests.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): target RTO = 10 minutes for capacity re-route; if we need reprovisioning across regions, up to 2 hours (but we offer burst cross-region where configured).
- Private (customer VPC/on-prem): RTO depends on customer infra; we supply runbooks and can run joint drills.

RPO: 
- Control plane metadata: <= 60 seconds (continuous replication).
- Customer data persisted to their storage (if integrated): depends on chosen persistence; by default we replicate config + checkpoints every 5 minutes.
- In-flight session/KV cache: best-effort, may be lost — call this out.

Backups: DB snapshots daily (7-day retention default), config backups every 24 hours, manual snapshot on major rollouts. Logs: 30-day retention by default (configurable).

Last DR test evidence: full control-plane failover test executed 2026-02-15 — end-to-end failover completed in 22 minutes (time to route, verify endpoints, smoke tests). I can attach the post-mortem and runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/dr-controlplane-2026-02-15.pdf

morgan-eng: For SIG wording, avoid heavy infra detail but give concrete numbers + where to find evidence. Suggested answer snippet for Q: "What is your RTO/RPO?" paste below and tweak as needed: 

```
Redwood provides differentiated RTO/RPO targets by deployment class. For our hosted managed tier we aim for an RTO of 15 minutes (automatic routing to warm standby instances) and an RPO of <=60s for control-plane metadata. Dedicated/reserved pools have an RTO target of 10 minutes for intra-region failover; cross-region reprovisioning (if required) can take longer and is covered in our runbook. For private deployments RTO/RPO are dependent on customer environment and are validated during onboarding. Detailed evidence (runbooks and most recent failover test results) are available upon request.
```

jaime-sales: That phrasing looks good. Two asks: 1) Can we attach the post-mortem and a sanitized runbook PDF for Heartwood? 2) Can legal confirm we can share the exact timestamps from the test?

security-bot: SIG follow-up updated (Q12-Q15). Attached artifacts pending upload: dr-controlplane-2026-02-15-postmortem.pdf, dr-runbook-sanitized.pdf. (automation)

ryan-infra: Uploaded sanitized runbook and post-mortem to the secure share. Link: https://redwood-secure-share/heartwood/dr-evidence-1802506789 (access granted to @jaime-sales and @emily-sales). Post-mortem includes timeline, actions, and mitigation follow-ups.

emily-sales: Perfect — I'll drop the draft wording + links into the Heartwood vendor portal and note they'll get the sanitized runbook. @jaime-sales can you confirm we hold their Dedicated pricing for 7 days while they review? :thumbsup:

jaime-sales: Confirmed — 7-day hold OK. I'll mention the SLA numbers and the test date in plain English.

morgan-eng: One small technical caveat to include: warm standby behavior can vary by model size and KV cache hit patterns; recommend adding a single sentence: "Some transient in-session state (in-flight tokens or transient KV entries) may not be fully recoverable; persistent checkpoints are replicated."

emily-sales: Good call — I'll add that line. Closing action items: 
- ryan-infra: add runbook + post-mortem links to portal (done)
- morgan-eng: approve final SIG wording (please respond here)
- jaime-sales: confirm pricing hold text (please send final message to Heartwood)

morgan-eng: Approved. Final suggestion: include the date of the last drill and the duration in the vendor portal entry for credibility.

emily-sales: Done. Posting now and will ping if they ask for anything else. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
